features.feature_value: Focus on rejecting/affecting decisions when either version called for violence or harm toward a person/group or political side.
features.evidence_span: calling for violence or harm towards a person or group/ political side
features.rationale: The participant explicitly ties their decision influence to threat/violence cues rather than agreement.

features.feature_value: They rejected only when a post called for violence or implied violence; otherwise most content was acceptable.
features.evidence_span: only time i rejected a post is when it called for violence or it insinuated violence
features.rationale: They describe a narrow rejection criterion centered on explicit/implicit violence.

features.feature_value: Deemed decisions mainly by whether the post advanced an argument; harsh/demeaning content plus weak argument led to rejection, while mild caustic but plausible points were accepted.
features.evidence_span: whether they advanced an argument... But if the phrase was highly demeaning... failing to advance an argument, that led me to reject
features.rationale: The reflection ties keep/remove influence to argumentative productivity and how demeaning language interacts with it.

features.feature_value: Personal attacks and vulgarity were leading factors in evaluating posts.
features.evidence_span: personal attacks and vulgarity were the leading factors
features.rationale: The participant states the main cues used in evaluation are personal attacks and vulgarity.

features.feature_value: They usually kept posts, but removed those containing insults or very strong accusations; anything not expected in a respectful debate.
features.evidence_span: remove posts where people were insulted or very strong accusations were thrown... anything that I wouldn't expect to hear in a respectful debate
features.rationale: They provide a clear keep/remove rule based on insult/accusation intensity and respectfulness.

features.feature_value: Influence based on whether arguments were productive versus just attacks; name-calling seen as worsening discourse.
features.evidence_span: whether or not the arguments were productive, and whether or not the arguments were simply just attacks
features.rationale: They contrast two qualities of the pair content (productive argument vs personal attacks) as the basis for their decision.

features.feature_value: Kept posts when opinions were reasonable; denied when both opinions seemed to come from lack of education.
features.evidence_span: If the opinions were reasonable... only denied when I thought both opinions were from a lack of education
features.rationale: Their decision hinges on perceived reasonableness/credibility tied to perceived education.

features.feature_value: They struggled to balance views with appropriate language.
features.evidence_span: hard to balance the views with appropriate language
features.rationale: This reflects an influence driven by difficulty managing the relationship between content and wording.
